differences.title: 1. Configuration
differences.leftDesc: Traefik leverages dynamic configuration via providers (Docker, Kubernetes) and API, automatically updating routes and services without restarts, promoting agility.
differences.rightDesc: Envoy supports static configuration files or dynamic configuration via xDS APIs (Discovery Service), offering flexibility for complex, evolving routing and load balancing rules.

differences.title: 2. Service Discovery
differences.leftDesc: Traefik natively integrates with orchestration platforms like Docker and Kubernetes, discovering services automatically and configuring routing rules based on labels and annotations.
differences.rightDesc: Envoy relies on external service discovery mechanisms or the xDS API to fetch upstream cluster information, making it highly adaptable to diverse environments.

differences.title: 3. TLS Management
differences.leftDesc: Traefik simplifies TLS by automatically obtaining and renewing certificates using Let's Encrypt (ACME), managing certificates dynamically for defined domains.
differences.rightDesc: Envoy typically manages TLS certificates via external systems like HashiCorp Vault or manual configuration, providing robust control over certificate lifecycle.

differences.title: 4. Observability
differences.leftDesc: Traefik offers an intuitive dashboard for real-time traffic visualization and configuration inspection, alongside integrated Prometheus metrics and tracing support.
differences.rightDesc: Envoy provides extensive, fine-grained metrics, distributed tracing, and access logs, designed for deep operational insights in complex distributed systems.

differences.title: 5. Extensibility
differences.leftDesc: Traefik uses a middleware pipeline concept, allowing sequential application of various functionalities like authentication, rate limiting, and request modification.
differences.rightDesc: Envoy employs a sophisticated filter chain architecture, enabling granular control over request/response processing at different network layers.

differences.title: 6. Protocol Support
differences.leftDesc: Traefik has strong support for modern HTTP protocols including HTTP/3 (QUIC), making it a capable edge proxy for the latest web standards.
differences.rightDesc: Envoy excels in supporting HTTP/2 and gRPC, widely used in microservice architectures, offering advanced load balancing and routing for these protocols.

differences.title: 7. Target Use Case
differences.leftDesc: Traefik is known for its ease of use and quick setup, making it ideal for developers and smaller deployments, with a strong focus on simplicity.
differences.rightDesc: Envoy is a battle-tested, high-performance proxy designed for complex, large-scale distributed systems and service meshes, offering deep control and customization.
